title: A title part move dragged by hand on the timeline survives a restyle
goal: When someone drags one of a title part's own movement bars on the timeline (the Headline's Opacity, Position or Scale), that change is thrown away the next time anything about the title changes: retiming another part, a theme, the energy or intensity. Their edit should stay, or the bar should not be draggable in a way that gets silently undone.
notes: Reproduced 2026-10-17 by a core probe (Tests, deleted after): Keynote title, headline opacity motion retimed 3520->3220 ms via LayerMotion.retimed, then doc.retimeTitlePart(layerID:index:2,grab:.start,byMS:300): headline opacity back at MotionTiming(startMS: 3520, durationMS: 400). Cause: restyleTitle -> refitTitle recompiles every part (applyTitleDesign replaces motions for every property the design moves), so a direct edit of compiled keys is lost. Predates a-title-page-s-parts-each-have-their-own-labelle (any restyle did it), which makes it easier to hit. Options: store per-part overrides in the recipe, or route bar drags on a title part's compiled motions into the design (a part's in/out builds), or recompile only the part that changed.
acceptance: Drag the Headline's Opacity bar 0.3 s earlier, then drag the Subtitle's start later: the Headline's Opacity bar is still where it was dragged
The same holds after changing the title's theme, energy and intensity
A walk does the drag, the restyle and the check at Next defaults
The same holds for an animated chart: a key or effect set by hand on one bar survives changing the chart's numbers or theme

log.note: digest 2026-10-18: same fault, second place. The animated charts audit (queue/audits/2026-10-17-animated-charts.json, rough) says changing a chart's data or theme lays its pieces out again and a key or effect set by hand on one bar is lost. Both are built pieces being rebuilt from their recipe and throwing away what the person did by hand, so one fix should cover both. Acceptance widened.

review before: a Premiere/AE user expects a keyframe bar they dragged to stay put when they restyle; the risk was a trim being mistaken for a hand drag (a trim leaves keys where they were), so the recipe now records the stretch it was keyed over (keyedOver) and hand moves are read against that. Slides key absolute positions, so keeping a dragged motion whole would strand it after a relayout: a timing-only edit re-applies its timing to the freshly compiled keys; any other key edit is kept whole.

built: Sources/PhotonzCore/TitleHandMoves.swift (handMoves/putBack, LayerMotion.movesLike), refitTitle wires it, ChartPen.rebuilt carries a bar's own keys and the effects its old drawing did not give it. Tests: TitleHandKeysSurviveRestyleTests (9), full suite 13750 green. Walk a-dragged-part-bar-survives-a-restyle-walk green; with putBack disabled it fails at the Subtitle drag (keys back at 3500-3920). expectRowKeys gained keptSince. Related walks green: title-part-rows-retime, title-knobs-restyle, title-set-keynote-clean, picked-row-drag-moves-whole-path. animated-charts-walk fails at a Library double click, already failing in the 2026-10-19 sweep and owned by walks-that-fail-in-the-full-sweep-26.

left rough: on a chart an effect the drawing gave a bar that the person then edited (not added) still goes back to the theme's on restyle; nobody asked, so it stays here. Looked at 3-restyled-sc.png: Sunset theme, Punchy, Intensity 35 in the panel, title restyled. Filed a-title-part-row-shows-where-its-hand-dragged-mo for the part row still drawn from the design.

A title part's movement bar dragged by hand (and any key edited by hand) survives retiming another part, theme, font pair, energy and intensity; chart bars keep their own keys and added effects through new numbers and themes. Core: TitleHandMoves.swift + refitTitle + ChartPen.rebuilt. Verified by TitleHandKeysSurviveRestyleTests (9, full suite green) and a-dragged-part-bar-survives-a-restyle-walk at Next defaults (fails with the fix disabled). Audit queue/audits/2026-10-19-a-title-part-move-dragged-by-hand-on-the-timelin.json.
